newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends lower in thin trade.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended a quiet session lower on Wednesday as concerns eased of heat stress to crops in the U.S. South, traders said.
"The rice has had a respite from the heat," a trade source said. He added that temperatures in key southern growing regions had moderated on Wednesday with highs mostly in the 80s Fahrenheit.
But there was some talk of lower-than-expected yields from early harvested crops in Louisiana. One trader said initial yields were about 20 percent below expectation.
International weather continued to garner attention.
Traders pointed to news the Philippines had gained permission to import 350,000 tonnes of rice due to threats of a drought.
The weather bureau there has predicted a drought in the Philippines starting in the last quarter of this year because of El Nino and said it could be the worst in 16 years.
Rice ended five to nine cents per cwt lower with September down five at $9.60. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 150 lots, against Tuesday's actual volume of 930 lots.
